articles.title: Real Madrid put injured duo on specific recovery plans to avoid relapses
articles.summary: Real Madrid are set to welcome Real Sociedad to the Santiago Bernabeu for their first La Liga home game of the season.Los Blancos are coming into this game w...
articles.body:
Real Madrid are set to welcome Real Sociedad to the Santiago Bernabeu for their first La Liga home game of the season.

Los Blancos are coming into this game with a 2-1 win against Espanyol behind them and will be hoping to put in a more cohesive performance against the Basque side.

Jose Mourinho will be without both Aurelien Tchouameni and Endrick against Sociedad, with the duo ruled out with injuries.

According to Diario AS , both players are following specific individual plans designed to prevent any relapse.

The key point is that their continued absence is being treated as part of a controlled process rather than an attempt to rush either player back into Mourinho's squad.

Tchouameni and Endrick have remained away from normal group work as Real Madrid carefully manage their respective recoveries.

Real Madrid star Aurelien Tchouameni is struggling with an issue since the World Cup. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images)

The objective is for both players to return only when they are physically ready to handle the demands of competitive football without increasing the possibility of another setback.

The cautious approach is understandable. The season has only just begun and Madrid have a long campaign ahead.

There is little to no value in accelerating a comeback for one league fixture and potentially losing the player for a long period.

Madrid have been guilty of rushing players back in recent seasons, which has seen injuries accumulate across the squad.

It looks like Jose Mourinho has learned a thing or two from the same and does not want to be in a position where he faces a similar injury crisis.

Tchouameni's absence is particularly notable because Madrid are still working out the ideal structure of their midfield under Mourinho.

Bernardo Silva and Federico Valverde started together in deeper roles against Espanyol, while Eduardo Camavinga provides another option.

Tchouameni, however, offers a more natural defensive presence at the base of midfield and could give Mourinho a different solution once fully fit.

Against a team like Real Sociedad who try to play through their opposition, the Frenchman's presence might have been helpful for Mourinho.

Carlos Espi and Endrick could compete for minutes behind Kylian Mbappe . (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Endrick faces a different challenge given the competition in attack. Kylian Mbappe is the first-choice striker up front, while new signing Carlos Espi has strengthened his case for minutes by scoring the winner against Espanyol.

The route to minutes is much more difficult for the Brazilian than it is for the French midfield star, but both will have to wait for their rehabilitation to be completed properly before they return to the pitch.

Once they recover and return to full fitness, both players could have important roles to play for Jose Mourinho, and it remains to be seen how the club handle their fitness in the coming weeks.

articles.body:
Reports in Italy claim that Aston Villa have decided against proceeding in negotiations for Milan winger Rafael Leao and that a move to fellow Premier League side Tottenham Hotspur is also looking unlikely.

Aston Villa decide against pursuing Leao deal

Milan are still seeking buyers for star winger Leao heading into the final few days of the summer transfer window.

PERTH, AUSTRALIA – AUGUST 05: Rafael Leao of AC Milan makes a run towards goal during the pre-season match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Optus Stadium on August 05, 2026 in Perth, Australia. (Photo by James Worsfold/Getty Images)

The Portugal international had made it clear at the end of the 2025-26 season that he felt this would be the right time to move on from Milan after spending the last seven seasons in San Siro, helping the team to their most recent Scudetto in 2021-22.

Leao has a €175m release clause in his contract, but with two years left on his deal and given that he has been seeking an exit and given that Milan are prepared to let him leave, the most recent suggestion is that the Rossoneri are seeking an offer in the region of €50m.

A few days ago, there had been reports that Premier League club Aston Villa were interested in pulling off a late deal with Milan, however, Wednesday's reports from La Gazzetta dello Sport claim that Unai Emery's side have decided to pull out of talks with the Rossoneri.

DUBLIN, IRELAND – NOVEMBER 13: Rafael Leao of Portugal reacts after the team's defeat during the FIFA World Cup 2026 qualifier match between Republic of Ireland and Portugal at Aviva Stadium on November 13, 2025 in Dublin, Ireland. (Photo by Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

There had also been suggestions earlier this week that R oberto De Zerbi's Tottenham could still be a potential destination for Leao, but given that they have just invested for around €87m (£75m), that no longer appears to be the case either.

La Gazzetta dello Sport suggests that Galatasaray are now the only genuinely interested party in Leao and that they could return to the table with an improved offer in the coming days.

The transfer window in Turkey will remain until September 4, a few days later than the window in Serie A, which closes on September 1.

articles.title: O'Neill: 'I'm responsible for this one'
articles.summary: Celtic boss Martin O'Neill has admitted blame following his side's capitulation away to LASK Linz that sees the Scottish side drop down from the Champions Le...
articles.body:
Celtic boss Martin O'Neill has admitted blame following his side's capitulation away to LASK Linz that sees the Scottish side drop down from the Champions League to the Europa League.

After a 3-0 win at Celtic Park and taking a 21st minute lead in Linz, the Bhoys looked on course to return to Europe's premier competition. However, five unanswered goals from LASK meant that it was instead the Austrian side who booked their place in the Champions League.

"I'm responsible for this one," O'Neill said after the game in which they conceded 40 shots over 120+ minutes.

"Without a doubt. Naturally it took me a long time to get over the UEFA Cup final in 2003 but this was majorly disappointing.

"In the context of things, one was a final which it would have been terrific to win, this was a qualifying game which we should have been able to get through.

"We know that we are a million miles from the finished article. That's absolutely true. I think we thought that anyway."

Missing out on the Champions League is also a big blow for the Scottish champions.

"The qualification for the Champions League is major, it's major in every aspect," O'Neill continued.

"Financially, for prestige, but we have to pick ourselves up. That's my responsibility again to do that.

"I think I said last week that if you could qualify for the Champions League there would be players wanting to come on that basis.

"That's not going to be the case but we'll see. Tonight we came up well and truly short, particularly in the second half."

Celtic can try and put Tuesday night behind them on Saturday when they host Falkirk in a return to league duty.

articles.title: Former Barcelona forward lashes out at Julian Alvarez and entourage over transfer request: ‘Is he stupid?’
articles.summary: The growing tension surrounding Julian Alvarez’s future has now sparked a strong reaction outside Spain, with former Barcelona forward and 1998 World Cup win...
articles.body:
The growing tension surrounding Julian Alvarez 's future has now sparked a strong reaction outside Spain, with former Barcelona forward and 1998 World Cup winner Christophe Dugarry delivering a scathing assessment of the striker's handling of his situation.

Speaking on RMC SPORT (h/t AS ), Dugarry criticised both Alvarez and the people advising him, arguing that the Argentine's decision to express his desire to leave Atletico Madrid for Barcelona has made an already complicated situation even more difficult.

"The player and his entourage are idiots. How can you say 'I want to leave the club'? Is he stupid or what?", he said.

The former France international's criticism was directed primarily at the public nature of the situation.

In Dugarry's view, a player seeking a move should approach such a sensitive situation with greater caution, particularly when dealing with a club and fans who could feel betrayed by a public declaration of intent.

Alvarez should have handled it differently

For Dugarry, Alvarez's mistake was not necessarily wanting a new challenge.

Rather, the former striker acknowledged that players should be able to pursue a departure when they genuinely wish to leave.

Christophe Dugarry has lashed out at Julian Alvarez and his representatives. (Picture credit: Stu Forster/Allsport)

His issue lies in how the Barcelona transfer situation has unfolded.

Dugarry pointed to Antoine Griezmann 's previous experience as an example of the risks involved when a player's future becomes a public dispute involving Atlético Madrid.

"Keep quiet, be modest, be smart about how you communicate.

"Didn't you see what happened with Griezmann? Don't you know your club's management? Don't you know your fans?" he pointed out.

Dugarry did not limit his criticism to the Argentine forward. He also questioned the role played by the people around the player, including his representatives and advisers.

Julian Alvarez wants to leave Atletico Madrid . (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

"And what about your entourage? Your agent? All the people around you?

"What's the point of them? What a huge mistake to go around saying publicly that Barça is your dream," he said.

Players should be allowed to leave, but…

Despite his harsh words, Dugarry did make an important point. He does not believe that a player should be forced to remain at a club against his wishes.

Instead, he argued that the manner in which a player pursues a transfer can determine whether an agreement becomes easier or harder to achieve.

"The first thing you have to do when you want to reach an agreement is not to spit in the face of your fans or your club," he concluded.

articles.title: 4 sleepers for college football national championship (but no 'next Indiana')
articles.summary: There’s no next Indiana, but there are sleeper teams for college football national championship.
articles.body:
There's no next Indiana . Let's set that straight from the start and frame this conversation properly.

To replicate Indiana's outhouse-to-penthouse rise, a longtime loser like Northwestern would need to ascend to the throne within a couple of years.

A more realistic debate would be this: Is there a team ranked outside the top 10 in the US LBM Coaches Poll that could replicate what the 2025 Hoosiers did and go from underrated to national champions?

Until Indiana, not since 2013 Florida State (preseason No. 12) had a team won the championship that wasn't ranked in the preseason top 10.

Who will win each conference? Record predictions for every FBS team in 2026

Where do champions come from? History tells us preseason No. 1 comes with warning

So, that's the framework for our exercise. Which teams not in the top 10 have the best chance — a longshot chance, perhaps, but a chance — to win the national championship?

This is why I say no "next Indiana" exists, because Lane Kiffin and LSU winning a national championship — the Tigers already have three national titles this millennium — would not be equivalent to Indiana overcoming a doormat's history to win a national championship, two years after hiring James Madison 's coach. But if we're purely looking at teams outside the top 10 with the goods to chase a ring, LSU must be on the list. Kiffin's portal haul is tremendous, and he's proven he can blend transfers. If quarterback Sam Leavitt ignites, LSU can't be ignored.

If there was ever a time for Lincoln Riley to break through at USC, this is it . No team returns more starters than USC, and although Dante Moore and Julian Sayin magnetize a lot of the hype surrounding Big Ten quarterbacks , USC's Jayden Maiava is star, too. USC's schedule is loaded — it includes Ohio State, Oregon and Indiana — but Riley should be able to compete with this roster. If he can't, maybe he's not the guy the Trojans thought they were getting.

The Brendan Sorsby saga overshadowed that Texas Tech remains the Big 12 frontrunner. Conference peers will struggle to score against a defense with a disruptive front and linebacker Ben Roberts in the middle of it all. The schedule is a breeze — No. 24 Houston is the only ranked opponent — so the Red Raiders are a good bet for the playoff. What do they achieve if they get there? Last season, they got shut out in a whimpering playoff loss. To be championship contenders, Will Hammond must become a better quarterback than Texas Tech thought he'd be. Otherwise, why did it try so hard to make a gambling addict its starter? If Hammond overdelivers, then Texas Tech is underrated.

From No. 19 to champions? Pretty extreme, right? Well, not for 2025 Indiana, and here's another Big Ten team lurking on the 19-line with an ace quarterback in Demond Williams Jr. He's got an offensive line full of familiar faces in front of him. There's good reason for skepticism that Washington will ascend past last year's 9-4 record, particularly because it must replace several defensive starters. But, the cliché rings true that if you've got a quarterback, you've got a chance, and Washington has a quarterback .

Blake Toppmeyer is the USA TODAY Network's senior national college football columnist. Email him at BToppmeyer@gannett.com and follow him on X @btoppmeyer .

articles.title: Monmouth football 2026 preview, roster breakdown, season prediction
articles.summary: The Hawks have a path to the FCS playoffs if they can live up to their potential on the gridiron this fall.
articles.body:
WEST LONG BRANCH -- There was theme among the songs that blared through the speakers at Kessler Stadium as Monmouth football practice got started Tuesday morning: Tennessee.

The Osborne Brothers' classic rendition of Rocky Top was the soundtrack for the opening stretches. It's a reminder that this is no longer training camp, it's game week. There are just a few days until No. 23 Monmouth will travel to Cookeville to take on No. 15 Tennessee Tech in a rare season-opening matchup of top 25 teams in the FCS. And the Hawks didn't waste anytime beginning to attack that challenge, going straight from stretch lines to 11-on-11 reps of hurry-up offense.

"It's a group that's got something to prove," Monmouth head coach Jeff Gallo said. "This team has something to prove as a collective unit. It's got talent, it's got ability, but it's about our ability every day to keep elevating the standard of our program and push that championship level on a daily basis."

No. 23 Monmouth football vs. No. 15 Tennessee Tech in Week 0: preview

The Hawks' first matchup is a chance to prove that they are at that championship level—or that more work is needed to reach it. Monmouth is on the national radar once again with a preseason top 25 ranking, but that could quickly slip away with a loss, or surge dramatically with a win.

After previewing the matchup with Tennessee Tech , it's now time to set the table for the Hawks' 2026 season as a whole. And that starts by looking back at the preseason epilogue to the many chapters of the regular season. With a wealth of experience as an offensive coordinator and an organized succession plan, Gallo was able to hit the ground running as a first-year head coach.

"You're constantly learning in any position you're at," Gallo said. "So you're setting a schedule, it's all new to you (as a head coach). Even if some of the things were the same as you did in the past, it's doing new things with people I know. And I was actually reflecting on it yesterday, wow, the second time through I'll already have the layout of how exactly I want to do it , and I can continue to make small adjustments and fine tunes."

It's those types of small revelations that feel thematic for this year's Monmouth football team. It's not entirely new for many of the core players, but the scale is undeniably larger. There are realizations and learning moments along the way that, combined with prior experience, could be the perfect formula to keep the team on a steady growth trajectory throughout the year.

Senior Gavin Nelson is one of several players that further encapsulates the fascinating middle ground between fresh novelty and veteran experience. He exploded in last year's season opener against Colgate with a career-high 176 receiving yards and three touchdowns, but Monmouth's deep receiving room meant a rotation of standout performances. Now in his final season, Nelson is ready to lead the room as a captain and preseason All-CAA selection.

"It's just the work you put in day-by-day when no one's watching," Nelson said. "The more work you do, it's just going to show out on Saturdays."

The element that could push this group over the top is motivation, and there's no shortage of source material. Monmouth finished 23rd in the country last season after a home upset loss to Albany derailed the team's playoff hopes.

"This team is hungrier than last year's team cause we fell short of the playoffs" Nelson said. "This team is more hungry and we've got a lot to prove this year."

It isn't just the anger and frustration of last year that is driving the Hawks, it is also love and loss. In the wake of first-year defensive coordinator Louis DiRienzo Jr.'s sudden death at 34 in late June, the team is embracing the stakes that come with a deep motivation to honor the coach who laid the foundation for an emerging defensive turnaround.

"We have a whole other purpose now. We're trying to really use the season to honor coach Louis D and rally together," Gallo said. "That's another big part of this: guys tightening this team and putting it together to honor what great coach and person he was."

It's a reminder of the humanity of a sport that is so often easily quantified into X's and O's. Those elements are worth analyzing and will be discussed in detail in this season preview. But Monmouth's key to success this fall goes beyond the schemes conjured up and the athletes that execute them on the gridiron. It's appropriate that this year's team is shaping up to be less star-driven and more depth-driven in 2026.

"This will be a hard-working team," Gallo said. "It might not be as flashy at times, but it's talented. It's gonna come from different places. I want our identity to be the toughest, tightest team in the country."

To be clear, Gallo has not named a starter and that may be a bit of gamesmanship that could go right up until gametime against Tennessee Tech, which has also not named a starting quarterback. But Weaver has steadily seen an increase in his share of practice reps and looks settled in with more consistency in his play. That being said, Seiss is always showing flashes like he did with deep touchdown throw on a corner route on Tuesday. With a top 25 matchup to open the season, it make sense to lean into the stability and experience of Weaver.

These positional breakdowns won't be as in-depth as the estimated depth chart from earlier this month, but some groups do require more context. One of the bigger changes between this year's team and last year's team is the committee approach to how the running backs will be utilized. In 2025, Rodney Nelson essentially accounted for around 75% of the team's rushing offense (while trying to exclude quarterback sacks which count towards the totals), but the Hawks will be more balanced with a stable of capable options in the backfield.

Jennings and Smith are poised to be the top two options, but it appears both Treadwell and Greg Randall will be in the mix in certain situations and offensive packages. The 6-foot-1 and 225-pound Treadwell will mark the return of Monmouth's signature power compliment that had been a staple of past teams. Randall has been one of the underrated stories of camp, carving out a role as a well-rounded back that is a capable runner but an exceptional receiver and pass blocker.

This is the first positional group that requires a bit more contextualizing in terms of the layout on the depth chart. The two proven returners from last year, Nelson (514 receiving yards with six touchdowns) and Neal (427 yards with seven touchdowns) appear firmly entrenched as the top two options. Harrison has separated himself with an outstanding camp and seems to be the clear third option, but that spot can be rotated in any number of ways with Newsome, Mister and Dorsey. It's also worth noting that when Nelson and Neal were at times limited in practice in the spring and fall, it was Harrison that usually stepped in.

After increasingly utilizing the wrinkle last year, Monmouth will not be shying away from 12 personnel (one back and two tight ends) this fall. Middleton is preseason All-CAA honoree that is the team's obvious candidate to be a breakout star after modest production behind Jack Neri last year. What's really exciting is the team's rapid introduction of Greg Genross, a transfer from West Virginia. The 6-foot-7 pass catcher is a startling presence on the field and gives the team flexibility as he can line up out wide as an "F" or as an in-line tight end. Garrett is the classic "H" type that is reliable as a blocker and pass catcher, so he should see plenty of playing time as well.

The offensive line experienced turnover at both tackle spots and both guard spots, but it's been a pretty steady top group from the spring into the fall. Fries and Duran have a lot of upside as a more athletic pairing at left and right tackle, respectively. Shriner is the lone returning starter at center, but Petito also brings a good amount of game experience at right guard. Goetter is the breakthrough performer of the group after a strong spring and fall. The key caveat with the presentation of the depth chart is that Reed Collins, a graduate transfer from Lafayette, will be the team's sixth offensive lineman and the sort of universal backup because of his versatility. He can line up at guard or tackle, and has the experience to potentially even push for a starter role as the season unfolds.

The defensive line might require the most explanation of any group. There's stability at the top as Watson and Rooks are two staples that lead the way, but there is going to be variety of different combinations deployed across the front. Lewis, Bigos and Johnson-Wilson are top of the rotation at defensive tackle. Acheampong is a player who can line up inside or outside.

The collection of edge rushers is one of the team's most intriguing storylines. Keshen has fully transitioned from linebacker to edge, which is understandable after he starred in the spring showcase. Former Wall standout Jake Davis, a transfer from Penn, is another reliable and experienced presence that is well-rounded as a run defender and pass rusher. That leaves Dyson and Lesaine, who have as much upside as anyone on the defensive line. They're both FBS transfers (Dyson from UMass and Lesaine from Syracuse) with incredible athleticism, but have been hampered by injury.

This group is one of the key inflection points on the roster. If the edges in particular thrive, Monmouth could make another leap forward on defense.

The "traditional" linebacker positions are set. Kishbaugh, Russo and Sasso are the top rotating pieces (although Alexander has been making strides). Kishbaugh is probably the biggest staple of the group as a stalwart against the run and the pass, so he will be a cornerstone presence in the middle even on subpackages.

The hybrid position known last year as "Viper" with Justin Bennin in the role has evolved slightly, but will still be a box safety position fundamentally. Delaware transfer Hasson Manning has stepped into that role and for good reason given he appeared in every game over his career with the Blue Hens, including nine starts in 2024.

Palmer returns after arguably being the team's best corner as a true freshman last season, although he's likely to step into the "boundary" role with less safety help as the team's top cover guy. Opposite him is an intriguing ongoing battle that still doesn't appear to be totally settled. Mathis is a massive 6-foot-4 corner that would give the Hawks an imposing pair of cover guys on the perimeter, but Haskett is more experienced with two starts at Richmond last year and brings a different type of physicality as an exceptional tackler. Along with edge rusher, this is one of the most intriguing positions to monitor early in the season.

There's not a lot to rehash with these last two spots on defense. Jones was an All-American as a sophomore and is the preseason CAA defensive player of the year. Fey has been a breakout performer in fall camp and quickly seized the spot opposite Jones. One note is that the safeties are shifted around a lot, but it does seem like Fey operates a little more at high safety with his length at 6-foot-2 being a valuable asset.

There's actually a bit to discuss here. Schabel returns as punter and would have ranked 40th in the FCS with his average of 41.8 yards per punt, but Monmouth only punted 25 times last year so he didn't chart on the NCAA's official stats. But kicker is naturally the most intriguing spot. Both Sholder and Graham have looked like an improvement at the position and there's a slight edge to the transfer from Delaware, but there's a battle brewing. Graham has looked comfortable with field goals up to 50 yards.

Aug. 29: at Tennessee Tech - 7 p.m. EST - ESPN+

Sept. 5: vs. Sacred Heart - 2 p.m. - FloSports

Sept. 12: at Western Michigan - 6:30 p.m. - ESPN+

Sept. 19: at Albany - 3:30 p.m. - FloSports

Oct. 17: at New Hampshire - 1 p.m. - FloSports

Oct. 24: at Hampton - 2 p.m. - FloSports

Oct. 31: vs. Bryant - 12 p.m. - FloSports

Nov. 7: vs. North Carolina A&T - 12 p.m. - FloSports

Nov. 14: vs. Merrimack - 12 p.m. - FloSports

Nov. 21: at Campbell - 12 p.m. - FloSports

Hardest games: Tennessee Tech, Sacred Heart, Western Michigan, Dartmouth, New Hampshire

It's certainly not a hot take to project a repeat of last year's record, but crucially Monmouth's non-conference slate should provide a boost and this projects that the Hawks go 7-1 and are in the FCS playoff conversation once again with better chances.

This is still more of an approximation than a game-by-game prediction, but Monmouth has a favorable conference schedule. A rough estimate of results is that between the Hawks' toughest non-conference games against Tennessee Tech, Western Michigan, and Dartmouth, they get at least one win. Admittedly, that is pretty optimistic. It's difficult to be on the road in four of the first five games.

Even presuming two losses out of those three, it's hard to envision two losses in conference play. But where it swings is the home opener against Sacred Heart, a team that should not be underestimated although it's the Pioneers first year in the CAA. They went 8-4 in 2025 and prepared themselves for the challenging transition with games against playoff teams Lehigh, Montana and Villanova.

New Hampshire is the other obvious tough conference foe after the Wildcats toppled Monmouth at home and reached the FCS playoffs at the Hawks' expense. But UNH lost its head coach and quarterback plus a lot of other key contributors from that team that went 8-5.

Those are the swing games, but now comes the good news for Monmouth fans. The other seven teams on the schedule had a combined record of 21-63 last season. Only 6-6 Towson didn't have a losing record, and Albany infamously upset Monmouth in the season finale. Obviously those two represent the potential for trap games, but the Hawks have a path to the FCS playoffs if they can live up to their potential this fall.

articles.title: Why Barcelona target Julian Alvarez is not training with Atletico Madrid as transfer saga drags on
articles.summary: The forward is not feeling great.
articles.body:
Julian Alvarez is headline news again on Wednesday as he's not training with Atletico Madrid as Diego Simeone's side prepare to face Sevilla in La Liga.

The forward's absence will likely get the rumor mill all excited but the explanation given is that he's simply not feeling well and has a stomach upset.

Reporter Ruben Uria posted on X: "We have been able to confirm that the Argentine forward will not participate today in the Atlético de Madrid training session, scheduled for this morning. The Argentine will not train today with the team. Julián had a bad night and is suffering from an upset stomach."

Alvarez is undoubtedly going through a difficult time right now . He was whistled by Atletico fans at the weekend against Villarreal after asking for a transfer at the World Cup.

Atletico Madrid refuse to sell the forward , despite his desire to move on, but Barcelona continue to monitor the situation in case Los Colchoneros decide to change their stance before the window closes next week.

The latest updates have suggested that Barcelona won't now sign an alternative to Alvarez as they haven't been convinced by any alternatives and remain determined to land the Argentina international.

articles.title: 'No major damage' for Forfar player after game abandoned for neck injury
articles.summary: Forfar Athletic say Adam Livingstone has not suffered any major damage after  Tuesday's Challenge Cup match against Formartine United was abandoned because of a neck injury suffered by the defender.
articles.body:
Forfar Athletic say Adam Livingstone has not suffered any major damage after Tuesday's Challenge Cup match against Formartine United was abandoned because of a neck injury suffered by the defender.

Forfar led 1-0 when Livingstone was hurt in an aerial clash early in the second half.

He received treatment on the pitch and was subsequently taken to Ninewells Hospital in Dundee, where he stayed overnight.

"Following last night's injury, Adam was taken to Ninewells Hospital where X-ray results have not shown any major damage," Forfar said in a statement on Wednesday.

"Adam was kept in hospital overnight but we have been advised that, all being well, he should be allowed home later today."

articles.title: Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after crash
articles.summary: Raheem Sterling has been charged after being accused of dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen; Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court for a hearing on September 15; the 31-year-old does not have a club
articles.body:
Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said the charges followed a single-vehicle collision on the M3 southbound, near Minley interchange, on May 28.

The 31-year-old is accused of dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen.

The force said that no other vehicles were involved in the collision and no injuries were reported.

Sterling, from Berkshire, is due to appear at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court for a hearing on September 15.

He scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate's side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020. He came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut.

Sterling, who was born in Kingston, Jamaica, moved to Manchester City in 2015 and won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019. He left for Chelsea in 2022 but after falling out of favour spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal.

After leaving Stamford Bridge, Sterling joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of the season. He is currently without a club.

In the 2021 Queen's Birthday Honours, Sterling was made an MBE for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out strongly against racism on and off the pitch for several years.

It came amid controversy over England fans booing players taking the knee at matches as a gesture against intolerance.

articles.title: “This was majorly disappointing,” Martin O’Neill. “That’s my responsibility”
articles.summary: Martin O’Neill was prepared to take the blame for what was a shambles of a performance from his Celtic side in Linz last night…Martin O’Neill, Manager of Cel...
articles.body:
Martin O'Neill was prepared to take the blame for what was a shambles of a performance from his Celtic side in Linz last night…

Martin O'Neill, Manager of Celtic looks on during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 Play off round second leg match between LASK and Celtic at on August 25, 2026 in Linz, Austria. (Photo by Christian Bruna/Getty Images)

Speaking to broadcaster for the night Amazon Prime the Celtic manager was asked to react to the game in which his side threw away a 4-0 aggregate advantage to lose 5-1 on the night and 5-4 on aggregate to crash out of the Champions League.

Kasper Hogh of Celtic reacts after the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 Play off round second leg match between LASK and Celtic at on August 25, 2026 in Linz, Austria. (Photo by Christian Bruna/Getty Images)

"It's very difficult to do that just after the game is over," O'Neill said. "We should have been out of sight by half-time. We scored a goal which was great, we missed two great opportunities, and then we give them a lifeline just before half-time and then one just after it.

"And they come roaring back and obviously we conceded from our viewpoint, not very good goals at all. That's my team and that's my responsibility."

He continued. with his post-match assessment: "Again, I'd have to say at half-time even though we've conceded a poor goal just before that, we were still well in command of the game.

"Just after half-time they score, then obviously momentum goes in their direction and it's hard to stem the point when they are chasing the game.

Celtic players pose for a team photograph before during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 Play off round second leg match between LASK and Celtic at on August 25, 2026 in Linz, Austria. (Photo by Christian Bruna/Getty Images)

"We tried to hold out for ten minutes and then we seemed to have weathered the storm as if we were going to see it through, then they score with a couple of minutes to go and that takes it into extra time.

"So really, obviously disappointed, disappointed that we've conceded the goals in the manner which we did. And again, I just go back to it's my team so I'm responsible for that," Martin O'Neill said.

Sebastian Tounekti of Celtic reacts after the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 Play off round second leg match between LASK and Celtic at on August 25, 2026 in Linz, Austria. (Photo by Christian Bruna/Getty Images)

The veteran Celtic boss then admitted that this defeat was one of his worst results as a manager and even more disappointing that the club's defeat in the 2003 UEFA Cup Final in Seville against Porto.

"I would say absolutely, yes. I put it up there before with the disappointment of losing the UEFA Cup Final in 2003, but tonight is so, so disappointing."

articles.title: WFISD football season opens with Memorial-Paschal Week 1 matchup
articles.summary: Memorial High School opens the 2026 football season against Fort Worth Paschal with a new head coach, new quarterback and key transitions on both sides.
articles.body:
Memorial High School opens its third varsity football season Thursday with a new-look offense, a new head coach and plenty of production to replace.

The Mavericks host Fort Worth Paschal at 7 p.m. at Memorial Stadium in the non-district season opener for both teams.

Memorial is coming off a 7-4 campaign that ended with a 28-14 loss to El Paso Andress in the Class 5A Division II playoffs. Former defensive coordinator Ross Dillard now takes over as head coach after helping guide the program through its first two varsity seasons.

Quarterback Joe Castles, running back Eric Powell and receiver Jamari Dean were all seniors last season. Castles threw 23 touchdown passes, Powell averaged 111.3 rushing yards per game and scored 18 total touchdowns and Dean averaged 95.9 receiving yards per game.

Senior Cole Birkhead now steps into the starting quarterback role after spending the previous two seasons as Castles' backup.

Memorial also returns some experience around him. Junior running back Gage Wuthrich rushed for 626 yards and seven touchdowns while averaging 8.8 yards per carry last season, giving the Mavericks a proven option as other players take on larger roles.

The defense will also transition, but Dillard's promotion gives Memorial continuity on that side of the ball. He spent the Mavericks' first two varsity seasons as defensive coordinator after nine seasons at Rider.

Senior linebacker and defensive end Reese Risner also returns after averaging a team-high 6.4 tackles per game last season.

Paschal should provide a solid first test. The Panthers finished 6-4 last season and return junior running back Truman Shelton, who rushed for 1,080 yards and 19 touchdowns as a sophomore.

Thursday offers the first look at how Birkhead settles in, how the defense responds under familiar leadership and how Memorial begins replacing several key contributors.
authors: Andy Mathis, Wichita Falls Times Record News

articles.title: López de Lerma: "Quiero un equipo protagonista con el balón, presionante y que genere muchas ocasiones"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Castilla repasa la actualidad del filial a cinco días del estreno liguero
articles.summary: El técnico del Castilla repasa la actualidad del filial a cinco días del estreno liguero
articles.body: El Castilla arranca la Liga el próximo lunes ante el Teruel (21.15 horas). Lo hará, como cada verano, tras una revolución en la plantilla, que ha perdido a Palacios, Fran González, Valdepeñas, Bruno Iglesias, Súnico, Loren Zúñiga, Manu Serrano y Jacobo Ortega, a la espera de salidas de última hora que apuntan a Manuel Ángel, David Jiménez, Cristian David o Lamini Fati. Al frente del equipo estará Julián López de Lerma, que afronta su primer proyecto al frente del renovado filial tras cogerlo a mitad de la temporada pasada. El técnico tendrá el reto de pelear por un ascenso que se le resiste al filial y que el año pasado volvió a rozar, cayendo en las semifinales del playoff para subir a Segunda. Julián repasa la actualidad del equipo en una entrevista con RMTV a cinco días del debut liguero. “Quiero ver el equipo lo más completo posible. Somos el Real Madrid y vamos a tener intención de ser protagonistas con balón, de ser un equipo presionante y de intentar generar muchas ocasiones. Sabemos de la dificultad del grupo y queremos estar preparados para momentos donde nos tocará sufrir un poquito más”. “Queremos ver el equipo con una identidad propia del Real Madrid Castilla, que es la que hemos visto durante todos estos años. Pero también estar preparados para, en esos momentos de dificultad que nos va a exigir la Primera Federación, que seamos el equipo más completo posible para para poder competir en los diferentes registros”. “Soy un entrenador exigente, cercano con el jugador. Llevo muchos años trabajando a nivel formativo y creo que eso es importante, sobre todo si trabajamos en un filial como el Real Madrid Castilla, donde entendemos que tenemos que sacar todo ese potencial que tienen los jugadores". “Es un grupo con equipos históricos, con equipos con grandísimos proyectos, con grandes ciudades detrás y con filiales también importantes. Es bueno para los chicos, para nosotros y para el equipo poder competir en partidos tan exigentes, porque eso es lo que va a hacer mejor este club”. “Este es un club de máximos y lo primero que tenemos que hacer, el primer objetivo, es ganar la jornada uno. La ambición y la ilusión es máxima. El Teruel ha cambiado de entrenador este verano y está claro que, jugando en casa, seguramente se van a hacer fuertes. Nosotros sabemos de la dificultad de jugar cualquier partido en esta competición fuera de casa, pero lo afrontamos con muchísimas ganas, con muchísima determinación de ir a por el partido y con la ambición que caracteriza a este club”. “Estamos muy contentos por lo que tenemos, por los jugadores y sobre todo por la ambición y por las ganas que han mostrado toda esta pretemporada y que seguramente que la seguirán mostrando durante el resto de temporada”.

articles.title: Ulisses García muy cerca de fichar por el Racing
articles.standfirst: Viene a reforzar el puesto de lateral izquierdo donde de momento tan solo está Jorge Salinas
articles.summary: Viene a reforzar el puesto de lateral izquierdo donde de momento tan solo está Jorge Salinas
articles.body: El Racing trabaja contrareloj para cerrar la plantilla antes del cierre del mercado. Después de hacer oficial la llegada de Matteo Prati en calidad de cedido, el siguiente en recalar en la escuadra cántabra puede ser el lateral izquierdo Ulisses García que milita en el Olympique de Marsella. Este futbolista tiene 30 años, es de nacionalidad suiza aunque nacido en Portugal. Ulisses García Grasshopers, Werder Bremen, Nuremberg, Young Boys, Olympique de Marsella y la pasada campaña jugó cedido en el Sassuolo donde coincidió con Pedro Felipe. En el primer encuentro de la Ligue 1 ha sido suplente y no ha disputado minutos. El curso anterior, en el Sassulo, jugó trece encuentros desde que arribó en enero. En ellos, anotó un tanto y aportó dos asistencias a sus compañeros. Además, a lo largo de su carrera ha jugado quince encuentros en la Liga de Campeones. Dos con el Marsella y el resto, con el Young Boys. Ulisses García viene a reforzar el puesto de lateral izquierdo donde de momento tan solo está Jorge Salinas, aunque hay muchas opciones que el futbolista cántabro acabe saliendo antes del cierre del mercado.

articles.title: El rojiblanco Javier Boñar será uno de los relevos de Arnau en el Girona
articles.standfirst: El lateral derecho del Atlético pasa reconocimiento médico y fichará por los catalanes, que también pretenden a Mateu Morey
articles.summary: El lateral derecho del Atlético pasa reconocimiento médico y fichará por los catalanes, que también pretenden a Mateu Morey
articles.body: El Girona tiene que acelerar los operaciones que tiene en marcha porqué el tiempo se le echa encima. Los blanquirrojos están pendientes de dar salida a Arnau Martínez, ya en la Ciudad Deportiva del Valencia para pasar reconocimiento médico y firmar su nuevo contrato; a Tsygankov, en Amsterdam; a Minsu, en Glasgow; y a Ounahi, Van de Beek y quién sabe si alguno más 'deshojando la margarita'. Con las salidas a punto, la dirección deportiva empezará a dar forma a las llegadas y la primera que se espera es la de Javier Boñar, canterano del Atlético de Madrid, por el que pagarán 2 M€ por el 50% de sus derechos del lateral, que firmará por cuatro años priorizando el proyecto de futuro del Girona antes que otras ofertas de primer nivel, como bien avanzó Matteo Moretto. Boñar, que ha competido con el Atlético Madrileño las últimas tres campañas y debutó con el primer equipo en el tramo final de la liga pasada, está pasando la revisión médica y en las próximas horas será anunciado como nuevo jugador para Quique Álvarez, que también desea un segundo lateral más formado y de rendimiento inmediato como Mateu Morey. El futbolista balear termina contrato el próximo junio de 2027 y quiere la carta de libertad o un traspaso simbólico, pero el Mallorca no ve claro reforzar a un rival directo en la lucha por el ascenso con el lateral derecho de Petra. Por otro lado, el coreano Minsu está a punto de ser jugador a todos los efectos del Glasgow Rangers. El club escocés abonará al contado los 10 millones de la cláusula del media punta que destacó el curso pasado en el Andorra y durante la pretemporada en el Girona. La pérdida de un jugador titular para Quique Álvarez obligará a maniobrar a la dirección deportiva, y más si Ounahi se marcha, algo que dejará la zona del ataque y el extremo zurdo despoblado.

articles.title: El Bolonia se entromete por Vargas
articles.standfirst: En Italia colocan al club ‘rossoblù’ tras el suizo, que ya tiene un acuerdo con Olympiacos
articles.summary: En Italia colocan al club ‘rossoblù’ tras el suizo, que ya tiene un acuerdo con Olympiacos
articles.body: Mientras el Sevilla apura los plazos para aligerar la plantilla y reforzar las posiciones marcadas por Luis García Plaza, la salida de Rubén Vargas se ha convertido en la llave para desbloquear la última fase de la planificación. El traspaso del internacional helvético, por el que en Nervión piden 15 millones de euros, no solo dejaría una importante plusvalía en la entidad hispalense, donde recaló por 2,5 millones. Además, su marcha continuaría liberando el margen salarial necesario para poder acometer las siguientes incorporaciones. Aunque Vargas volvió del Mundial pensando en firmar por un equipo de Champions League, el que más ha pujado por su fichaje ha sido el Olympiacos, que disputará la Europa League. El acuerdo con el futbolista es total y las conversaciones entre ambos clubes están avanzadas, pero en esta recta final de la operación ha entrado en escena un nuevo actor. Según apunta el periodista Gianluca Di Marzio, el Bolonia ha preguntado por la situación del extremo suizo, al que considera la solución ideal para cubrir la inminente marcha de Jonathan Rowe a la Atalanta. La información añade que el equipo rossoblú podría presentar una oferta en las próximas horas. El Sevilla ha entrenado este miércoles en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, en una sesión donde la gran novedad ha sido precisamente el regreso de Rubén Vargas. El jugador trabajaba al margen desde el pasado viernes y no viajó a Bilbao para el partido contra el Athletic. "Con Rubén se está valorando una situación entre todos y no queremos asumir riesgos. Nos pasa a nosotros, es una de las cosas de tener mercado abierto mientras se vayan disputando partidos y se está valorando", comentó ayer el director deportivo, José Ignacio Navarro, que debe resolver cuanto antes el culebrón para rearmar el equipo antes del cierre del mercado.

articles.title: El Villarreal cierra el mercado con la cesión de Kambwala al Como
articles.standfirst: El franco congoleño jugará en Italia tras descartar la opción de jugar cedido en Osasuna
articles.summary: El franco congoleño jugará en Italia tras descartar la opción de jugar cedido en Osasuna
articles.body: El rocambolesco final de mercado protagonizado por Willy Kambwala ha tocado a su fin con su llegada al Como. El defensa franco congoleño jugará la próxima temporada en el conjunto italiano en calidad de cedido, toda vez que el cuadro transalpino se guarda una opción de compra para hacerse definitivamente con sus servicios al final de la misma. Con esta operación, que llega horas después de de confirmar el fichaje de Nathan Saliba, el conjunto amarillo da por cerrada su plantilla salvo sorpresa inesperada de última hora. Lo cierto es que la última semana del zaguero ha sido especialmente movida cuando todo hacía indicar que su futuro pasaba por el Sádar de Pamplona. Con excedente de centrales tras el regreso de Juan Foyth y la recuperación de Logan Costa, Kambwala pasaba a ser el quinto defensa del equipo, con lo que una salida en busca de minutos se presentaba como la opción más lógica para un defensa joven como es su caso. Y en ese contexto la petición del cuadro rojillo al Villarreal para el préstamo del futbolista, se presentaba como la opción ideal. Tras meditar la decisión durante varios días y con el acuerdo total entre entidades, el futbolista dio el pasado martes el visto bueno a una operación para la que faltaba poco más que la firma. Pero cuando en Pamplona esperaban su llegada, a última hora entró en escena el Como y el futbolista cambió radicalmente de idea. En cuestión de horas, este descartaba la opción navarra para alcanzar un acuerdo con los italianos, quienes podrían acabar a medio plazo Para explicar el giro de los acontecimientos hay una figura fundamental como es la del agente del futbolista: Darren Dein. El afamado intermediario británico, hijo del expresidente del Arsenal, David Dein, representa a ex “gunners” como Thierry Henry o Cesc Fábregas, actual entrenador del Como. En plena búsqueda de un central por parte de los italianos, el nexo de unión entre Fábregas y Kambwala es el de su agente común, quien ofreció la opción del futbolista del Villarreal y facilitó la operación. Tras su salida y salvo movimiento inesperado, el Villarreal cierra la puerta a más salidas.

articles.title: Vinculan a Morata… con el Leganés
articles.standfirst: Di Marzio apunta al interés pepinero, aunque la operación sería muy complicada
articles.summary: Di Marzio apunta al interés pepinero, aunque la operación sería muy complicada
articles.body: El nombre de Álvaro Morata ha aparecido vinculado de manera sorprendente al C.D. Leganés. Según una información del periodista italiano Gianluca Di Marzio, el conjunto pepinero estaría interesado en incorporar al delantero español esta misma temporada. Por el momento, desde el club madrileño no se pronuncian sobre estas supuestas negociaciones, por lo que la información debe tomarse con cautela. El gran obstáculo sería el elevado salario de Morata, muy alejado de los parámetros habituales del Leganés. Para que la operación pudiera llegar a buen puerto sería necesaria una importante aportación económica del Como, que tendría que asumir parte de la ficha del atacante. Una posibilidad sorprendente y de enorme repercusión, pero que, a día de hoy, se presenta muy complicada.

articles.title: Clemente vuelve y 'mete en un problema' a De la Barrera
articles.standfirst: Bonfanti y Herzog deberán luchar por un puesto en el centro de la zaga
articles.summary: Bonfanti y Herzog deberán luchar por un puesto en el centro de la zaga
articles.body: Las Palmas recupera a Enrique Clemente tras un mes lesionado. El defensa ya entrena con el grupo, lo que supone una excelente noticia para el equipo canario. El aragonés parte como indiscutible en el lateral izquierdo, una posición que durante su ausencia ha ocupado Bonfanti. Es decir, su vuelta podría provocar también movimientos en el centro de la zaga en efecto dominó. El italiano tiene la alternativa de actuar como central zurdo, una posibilidad que podría dejar fuera de la ecuación a Herzog. Pero también está la otra vertiente, esa que habla de que lo que funciona no se toca. El tinerfeño, que está demostrando un excelente nivel, asume la competencia como una parte natural del fútbol y este miércoles lo dejó claro en sala de prensa: "Es importante que exista competencia en la plantilla. Si no es así, el nivel baja y te acomodas. La competencia es buena para el equipo. El año pasado lo comprobamos con Alex Suárez y conmigo. Barcia y Mika Mármol estuvieron muy bien en parte por la competencia que había el año pasado". El otro foco está en la portería, donde Horkas pone punto final a su etapa como jugador amarillo. El guardameta se ha despedido de la UD Las Palmas con una carta cargada de emoción y sentimiento de pertenencia, dejando claro el vínculo que ha construido con el club y con la isla. "La UD Las Palmas fue mucho más que un lugar donde jugué al fútbol, se convirtió en mi casa. Aquí nació mi hijo", escribió el portero en su adiós. El croata cierra una etapa profesional y personal muy importante, además de dejar en el club 4.5 millones de euros.

articles.title: Man City to bid for Chelsea's Â£120m-rated Enzo Fernandez
articles.summary: Manchester City are set to make an opening offer for priority midfield target Enzo Fernandez.
articles.body:
Manchester City are set to make an opening offer for Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez.

The Argentina international has been identified by manager Enzo Maresca as a priority target to bolster City's midfield after a series of high-profile exits.

Chelsea are aware of City's interest and set an unofficial deadline for the deal to be completed earlier this summer at a minimum fee of Â£120m only for that date to pass.

Nevertheless, City are expected to return with another attempt to sign the 25-year-old before next week's transfer deadline.

Fernandez could become one of the most expensive signings in Premier League history, behind only Liverpool's Â£125m move for Alexander Isak last summer.

Fernandez maintains a positive relationship with Maresca, who left Chelsea in controversial fashion on New Year's Day and moved to Etihad Stadium in June.

It could potentially be the second time City break their transfer record in the same window having paid Â£116m to recruit Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest .

There have also been four major midfield departures, with Tijjani Reijnders sold to Saudi Arabian club Al-Qadsiah for Â£52m , while Barcelona have signed Rodri for Â£65m, Newcastle have agreed a Â£52m deal to sign Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva departed earlier in the summer before joining Real Madrid.

It has been a turbulent period for Fernandez at Stamford Bridge, during which he and his agent, former Paris St-Germain midfielder Javier Pastore, courted interest from Real Madrid, only for the Spanish club to issue a statement denying any attempt to sign him.

The situation has been ongoing since Chelsea were knocked out of the Champions League by PSG in March, after which Fernandez became increasingly critical of the club.

New Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso spoke in July about a private conversation he had with Fernandez, who signed for Â£107m from Benfica in 2023, but declined to disclose details of the discussion.

Fernandez came on as a second-half substitute in Monday's 3-2 win over Fulham and was booed by home supporters because of his role in England's World Cup exit.

After briefly celebrating with the away fans and his team-mates after the final whistle, he was the first Chelsea player to head down the tunnel.

Chelsea 's record sale is Eden Hazard's move to Real Madrid in 2019, which was worth an initial Â£89m plus add-ons taking it up to a potential Â£150m.

articles.standfirst: La aerolínea se convierte en nuevo patrocinador global
articles.summary: La aerolínea se convierte en nuevo patrocinador global
articles.body: Egyptair, la compañía aérea nacional de Egipto, ha firmado como 'Global Partner' (patrocinador global) del FC Barcelona hasta la temporada 2028-2029, según ha informado este miércoles la entidad catalana en un comunicado. En el marco de esta alianza, la compañía del país norteafricano se convierte, además, en "aerolínea oficial exclusiva" de la primera plantilla de fútbol masculino, así como de los equipos de baloncesto y de balonmano. Además, el conjunto de balonmano, entrenado por Carlos Ortega, lucirá el emblema de Egyptair en la parte frontal de la camiseta en sus partidos. Según precisa el club azulgrana en el comunicado, esta alianza "se enmarca en el plan de expansión de la flota y de la red de rutas internacionales de Egyptair y pone de manifiesto el compromiso de la compañía por mejorar sus servicios y ofrecer una experiencia de viaje superior". "Para el FC Barcelona, este nuevo acuerdo de patrocinio supone una oportunidad para ampliar el alcance global de la marca Barça, conectar con nuevos mercados y reforzar su posicionamiento como uno de los equipos deportivos con mayor capacidad de influencia en el ámbito internacional", añade el comunicado. Cabe recordar que el primer equipo de fútbol del Barcelona cuenta actualmente en sus filas con el jugador egipcio Hamza Abdelkarim, un delantero centro con ficha del filial que ha destacado en la pretemporada con cuatro goles en tres partidos amistosos. Egyptair, fundada en 1932, cuenta con una red internacional y doméstica que conecta Egipto con más de 85 destinos en África, Europa, Oriente Próximo, Asia y América del Norte.

articles.title: How Borussia Dortmund are trying to recreate the exciting BVB of the past as they rebuild with youth under Niko Kovac
articles.summary: Ahead of the return of the Bundesliga, Adam Bate visits Borussia Dortmund to speak to head coach Niko Kovac as well as players and executives to find out how the perennial challengers to Bayern Munich are returning to first principles in an attempt to win again...
articles.body:
"Four players left. We bought some new talented players and also one experienced player. So we kept the spine, the experienced players, the goalkeeper, the centre-back, the midfielder. And now we are trying to create the BVB, I would say, from the past."

That means the sort of talents who can thrill the fans packed onto that Yellow Wall, those able to play the rock-and-roll football that has defined Dortmund since the days of Jurgen Klopp. More counter-pressing, less control. Football with a bit more feeling.

Dortmund had drifted away from this core principle. The focus shifted to older signings. It was seen as an attempt to protect their position, prioritising the need to play it safe in an attempt to guarantee Champions League qualification. Not very Dortmund.

The experienced player Kovac refers to is Joey Veerman, a 27-year-old midfielder from PSV Eindhoven. But it is the acquisition of two Greek wingers, the eye-catching Giannis Konstantelias and the 18-year-old prospect Konstantin Karetsas, that has fans talking.

In the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup , the atmosphere inside Signal Iduna Park ignited when Konstantelias came on for the second half and started running at Bayern Munich's defence. Dortmund were desperately close to turning around a two-goal deficit.

Speaking to Julian Ryerson afterwards about his new teammates, the experienced Norwegian said: "It looks positive, yeah. We also had some good players last year but I hope it takes us to a new level, of course. I hope and I think that we are on a good path."

It will not be easy. Karim Adeyemi and Julian Brandt were proven in the Dortmund black and yellow. They are gone now. "We need to replace these goals, it is clear," says Kovac. "Of course, when you buy new players, you never know if it is going to work or not."

But perhaps that's part of the thrill. Dortmund are daring to dream once again, gambling on the potential for greatness, hoping for more. "Our expectations are high because we saw that, especially the offensive players, the two Greek ones, they have a big talent."

Is Kovac the man to coax out that talent? He is a proven winner but one who has something of a reputation for prioritising perspiration over inspiration so it will be fascinating to see whether he can provide the framework for these youngsters to thrive.

What is Niko Kovac football? When that question is put to the man himself, he admits it is something that he once asked a friend. His reply? Successful football. It is a fair point. Kovac won the cup with Eintracht Frankfurt and then the double with Bayern Munich.

But he knows that his particular brand is sometimes seen as limited compared to his more celebrated peers. Kovac has dabbled with inverting his wing-backs of late but his tactical tweaks are less likely to be pored over than those of Bayern's Vincent Kompany.

"If someone likes my style, this is up to you. For me, we are successful. And I think that, together, since we arrived, we did a very good job. As a coach, I think you need to see what kind of players you have, what situation you have, and you must always adapt."

That is exactly what Kovac did when he joined Dortmund in late January of 2025 with the club in a perilous position in the wrong half of the Bundesliga table. The team had completely lost its identity and looked in disarray, European qualification a long shot.

Speaking to Carsten Cramer about this, Dortmund's chief executive is clearly still grateful. "Imagine what happened when we hired him one-and-a-half years ago. We were in regions we never should be and he brought us to the Champions League."

Cramer adds: "He is committed. He loves to work for the club. Black and yellow fits him, I would say, much better than the red and white [of Bayern] or the green and white [of Wolfsburg]. I am 100 per cent sure that he is the right man at the right moment."

The credit that Kovac has in the bank is thoroughly deserved. "I arrived in a bad situation," he says. He changed things. "The squad was planned with a back four, but after two or three games we saw it was not working so we changed into the back five."

He adds: "This was from the tactical perspective. What was also obvious was that the physical capacities, how I see football, how I see a fully fit player, was not there. So we worked on this. With those physical abilities you're immediately a better football player."

His reasoning is that through improved fitness, the decisions on the pitch become easier. "Without those physical abilities, you are calculating. Should I run backwards? Should I run forward? Should I defend? Should I attack?" If you are fitter, you just do it.

"This was a little bit tricky because when it is not working players always fall into the same old habits, so it took a little bit of time. But we finished fourth." From there, Dortmund had a platform and they used it to finish in second spot again last season.

The gap to Bayern ended up being 25 points at the end of his first season. It reduced to 16 points last time around. When it is framed like this, a title challenge still feels some way off. "To close this gap, a lot must happen." Dortmund must play above themselves.

"It is also important that Bayern Munich is not playing top," he concedes. The frustration in the recent past is that chances have come and not been taken. They tossed a title away on the final day in 2023 and saw Bayer Leverkusen end Bayern's streak in 2024.

But the hope - always the hope - is that the fusion of his discipline with the high ceiling of the new talent means there are possibilities once more. Can they do it? "I do not like to speak first and then work," says Kovac, smiling. "I think the opposite way is better."

articles.title: Pellegrini, primer entrenador que alcanza las 100 victorias en Primera división con el Betis
articles.standfirst: El Ingeniero llegó anoche a una cifra redonda tras el triunfo verdiblanco en Mestalla
articles.summary: El Ingeniero llegó anoche a una cifra redonda tras el triunfo verdiblanco en Mestalla
articles.body: Manuel Pellegrini sigue haciendo historia en el Betis. En su séptima temporada consecutiva al frente del conjunto verdiblanco, el chileno se convirtió anoche en el primer entrenador que alcanza las 100 victorias en Liga en Primera división con el club de las Trece Barras. Lo hizo después de que su equipo se impusiera por 0-1 al Valencia en Mestalla, con un gol del canterano Pablo García en los minutos finales del partido. El Ingeniero alcanza los 100 triunfos ligueros como verdiblanco después de sentarse en el banquillo andaluz en 230 partidos en la competición doméstica. Es decir, su equipo ha sumado los tres puntos en LaLiga en el 43,47% de los partidos desde que está al frente. Sus registros se completan con 69 empates, un 30% del total, y 61 derrotas, apenas un 26,52% de los encuentros disputados. Unos registros que han permitido al Betis clasificarse seis veces seguidas para disputar competiciones europeas, récord absoluto en los casi 120 años de historia del club. Pellegrini se convierte así en el primer entrenador que llega a las 100 victorias ligueras con el Betis en una clasificación en la que le siguen Lorenzo Serra Ferrer, con 78 triunfos, Ferenc Szusza, con 46 victorias, Luis Cid Carriega, con 41, y Pepe Mel, con 36. Si sumamos todas las competiciones, el chileno se ha sentado en el banquillo bético en 313 partidos oficiales con un balance global de 147 victorias, 86 empates y 80 derrotas. Entre sus logros desde que aterrizó en Heliópolis, además de meter a su equipo seis veces seguidas en Europa, está el título de Copa logrado en la temporada 2021-22 y el flamante regreso a la Liga de Campeones más de dos décadas después que los verdiblancos disputarán esta temporada y cuyo sorteo de la fase de grupos se celebrará este jueves. Pellegrini está afrontando su última campaña firmada al frente del equipo, ya que su contrato expira el próximo 30 de junio y por el momento no hay noticias de una posible renovación.  * Datos de Documentación MARCA, Bdfutbol y Opta

articles.title: Arnau Martínez pasa el reconocimiento médico antes de firmar por el Valencia
articles.standfirst: El lateral derecho llegó de madrugada a la capital del Turia y espera ponerse a las órdenes de Corberán este jueves, tras el anuncio oficial
articles.summary: El lateral derecho llegó de madrugada a la capital del Turia y espera ponerse a las órdenes de Corberán este jueves, tras el anuncio oficial
articles.body: Arnau Martínez ya ha dado el último paso previo a su incorporación oficial al Valencia. El defensa catalán, que llegó de madrugada a la capital del Turia, ha completado el reconocimiento médico y queda pendiente únicamente de la firma de su contrato y del anuncio oficial por parte del club de Mestalla. El futbolista, de 23 años, se presentó a primera hora de la mañana en la Ciudad Deportiva de Paterna para someterse a las habituales pruebas médicas previas a su fichaje. Después, se trasladó al centro médico habitual en el que los jugadores completan las pruebas para la revisión. E lateral derecho firmará un contrato de larga duración que le vinculará al Valencia hasta junio de 2031. La operación pone fin a varias semanas de negociaciones entre el Valencia y el Girona que se cerraron en un traspaso de cinco millones de euros fijos, más uno en variables y un porcentaje sobre una futura venta del jugador. Arnau Martínez era una de las prioridades del técnico Carlos Corberán para reforzar la línea defensiva. Su polivalencia es uno de los factores más valorados por el cuerpo técnico, ya que puede actuar tanto de lateral derecho como de central marcador, que es la posición en la que comenzó hasta avanzado su proceso de formación, cuando Míchel -en el Girona- lo reubicó en la banda. No hay que olvidar que este martes debutó como titular en la posición de lateral derecho Pablo Maffeo. Formado en las categorías inferiores del Barcelona, la carrera de Arnau Martínez se ha desarrollado íntegramente en el Girona donde se había convertido en una pieza importante del conjunto catalán. A pesar del interés mostrado por otros clubes durante el mercado de fichajes, la voluntad del jugador de recalar en Mestalla resultó determinante para desbloquear la operación. Si no surge ningún contratiempo, el Valencia oficializará su incorporación a lo largo de las próximas horas. El objetivo es que Arnau Martínez pueda incorporarse este jueves a los entrenamientos y quedar a disposición de Corberán de cara al próximo compromiso liguero frente al Deportivo de La Coruña en Riazor.
